name: Root Cause Analysis Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday root cause analysis work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical root cause analysis tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday root cause analysis work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical root cause analysis tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting root cause analysis work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Measure before optimizing any root cause analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. When root cause analysis guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Prefer the simplest root cause analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
5. Keep root cause analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Validate root cause analysis outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to root cause analysis (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
8. When root cause analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. State assumptions about root cause analysis explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
10. Document any non-obvious root cause analysis decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of root cause analysis correctness.
- Do not apply generic root cause analysis advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop root cause analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new root cause analysis abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting root cause analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for root cause analysis, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
